set.question: Which sentence contrasts a past habit and the present?

Antes estudiaré por la noche, pero ahora estudio por la mañana. [I will study at night before, but now I study in the morning.]

old: Impersonal constructions describe learning processes without naming a specific learner. Spanish commonly uses *se*, *hay que* and *es necesario* to express general statements and conditions for learning.
new: You know impersonal *se* from B1 Unit 11 and *hay que* from A1 Unit 18; here you use them to talk about learning, together with *es necesario* + infinitive (*necesario* is A1 Unit 18). They describe learning processes without naming a specific learner and express general statements and conditions for learning.
why: Every structure on the screen is known; the screen presented them as new. Recap added.

set.question: Which expression gives a general obligation?
options: Hay que practicar todos los días. [You have to practise every day.]
Practico todos los días. [I practise every day.]
Practicaré todos los días. [I will practise every day.]

why: length-giveaway ERROR (18 vs 11); all options now share "todos los días" and are close in length; ds added for the real present and future forms; unmet "expresa, obligación" bracket removed.

old: Opinions can take the indicative when the speaker presents the proposition as asserted. Negative or uncertain expressions of opinion commonly trigger the subjunctive when the proposition is rejected or not asserted.
new: You know the present subjunctive after wishes, emotions and value judgments from A2 Unit 27. Opinions take the indicative when the speaker presents the idea as asserted (*creo que*, *pienso que*, *considero que*). A negative opinion (*no creo que*, *no pienso que*) takes the subjunctive, because the idea is rejected, not asserted.
why: Text promised "uncertain expressions" (subjunctive-doubt is B1 Unit 25) and had no recap of the known subjunctive.

old:
"spanish": "Es posible que este método sea eficaz.",
          "english": "It is possible that this method is effective."
new:
"spanish": "No pienso que este método sea eficaz.",
          "english": "I don't think this method is effective."
why: "Es posible que" is probability, taught with subjunctive-doubt (B1 Unit 25), not yet.

old: *Creo que* normally presents the following proposition as asserted. *No creo que* and expressions of uncertainty normally use the subjunctive.
new: *Creo que* presents the idea that follows as asserted: indicative. *No creo que* and *no pienso que* take the subjunctive.
why: Removes "expressions of uncertainty" (later skill).

set.question: Choose the correct contrast.
options: Creo que es útil, pero no creo que sea perfecto. [I think it is useful, but I don't think it is perfect.]
Creo que sea útil, pero no creo que sea perfecto. [I think it be useful, but I don't think it is perfect.]

old: Comparisons and evaluations show relative effectiveness. Spanish uses *más*/*menos*... *que*, *tan*... *como*, *mejor*/*peor* and superlatives to compare methods and judge their value.
new: You know *más*/*menos*... *que* and *tan*... *como* from A2 Unit 6. New here are the superlatives. The relative superlative uses *el/la/los/las más/menos* + adjective (+ *de*), and *mejor*/*peor* become *el/la mejor*, *el/la peor*. The absolute superlative says “very” with *-ísimo/-ísima*: *útil* becomes *utilísimo*.
why: Screen presented the A2 comparatives as new and showed only one superlative (la mejor opción); the skill is "relative and absolute superlatives". Recap added; absolute superlative named.

old:
"spanish": "Este método es tan útil como el anterior.",
          "english": "This method is as useful as the previous one."
new:
"spanish": "Esta es la estrategia más eficaz de todas.",
          "english": "This is the most effective strategy of all."
why: Known comparative example swapped for a relative superlative (the taught point).
Adds the absolute superlative the skill title promises.

old: Use *más*/*menos*... *que* and *tan*... *como* for comparison, and *mejor*/*peor* or superlatives for evaluation.
new: Use *el/la más* + adjective for the relative superlative, *el/la mejor* and *el/la peor* for good and bad, and *-ísimo* for “very”. Never say *más mejor*.
why: Tip now states the superlative rules.

new: You know *creo que* and *considero que* from this unit. Another way to give an opinion is *me parece que* + indicative: *me parece que la práctica es esencial*. To defend an opinion, give your position, a reason or evidence, and acknowledge another view before your conclusion.
